# RFC-0009: NSys static timeline visualization artifact contract

> **Version:** 0.2.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec

**References:** [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md), [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md), [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md), [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md), [RFC-0002:C-EXCEPTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-exceptions), [RFC-0005:C-ARTIFACT-ROOT](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-artifact-root), [RFC-0005:C-LEAK-SAFETY](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-leak-safety), [RFC-0002:C-SUCCESS-RESPONSE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-success-response), [RFC-0003:C-LIST-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-list-shape), [RFC-0004:C-COMMAND-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-command-surface), [RFC-0006:C-SUPPORTED-INPUTS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-supported-inputs)

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0009:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0009c-summary"></a>

This RFC specifies the NSys static timeline visualization artifact contract. It defines a source-owned command for exporting a bounded timeline window as an SVG figure, the machine-readable response shape that describes that figure, the track specification model used to request Nsight Systems-style timeline tracks, and the rendering constraints that keep the figure usable for agent-authored reports.

**Scope:** This RFC covers the NSys `viz timeline` command contract, track selector syntax, track tree resolution, SVG artifact ownership, render limits, label and minimum-width behavior, optional highlight semantics, and compatibility boundaries. It does not specify an interactive GUI, a notebook view, PyTorch visualization behavior, NCU visualization behavior, private renderer implementation types, private SQL helper layout, or pixel-perfect SVG styling.

**Rationale:** VeloQ already exposes structured evidence for agents, but final reports often need a compact visual timeline to communicate temporal alignment, idle spans, stream activity, annotation context, and a small number of dominant events. A static SVG artifact gives agents a report-ready figure while preserving VeloQ's CLI, JSON, artifact-lifecycle, and non-GUI boundaries.

*Since: v0.1.0*

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0009:C-COMMAND-SURFACE] Command surface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-command-surface"></a>

The NSys source MAY expose a `viz timeline` command while this RFC remains draft.

When stabilized, the NSys source command surface MUST identify the command as `nsys.viz.timeline` in the JSON envelope.

The `nsys viz timeline` command MUST accept one NSys-supported trace input.

The `nsys viz timeline` command MUST require a bounded time window.

The bounded time window MUST be expressible with `--from` and `--to` using the same time literal semantics as other NSys time-windowed commands.

The command MUST reject a missing lower or upper time bound with a structured diagnostic.

The command MUST reject an empty or negative time window with a structured diagnostic.

The command MUST accept one or more repeated `--track <spec>` arguments.

When no `--track` argument is supplied, the command MUST apply the default track set.

The default track set MUST include `gpu:device=all`.

The default track set MUST include `cuda-streams:device=all,top=<default_top_streams>`.

The default track set MUST include `gaps-overlay:device=all`.

The `<default_top_streams>` value MUST be a documented positive integer.

The default track set MAY include annotation tracks when the source evidence needed by those tracks is present in the trace.

The command MUST echo the resolved time window and resolved track set in its JSON response.

The command MAY accept `--out <path>` to direct the SVG artifact to a caller-selected path.

The command MUST keep stdout reserved for the primary response payload in JSON mode.

The command MUST NOT write the raw SVG to stdout in its default mode.

A future raw-SVG stdout mode MUST be documented as an explicit output exception before it is treated as stable.

**Rationale:** The command is a figure export, not an interactive viewer. Requiring a bounded window prevents accidental full-trace rendering, repeated `--track` keeps agent-generated commands explicit, and the JSON envelope preserves the existing machine-readable contract.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-TRACK-SPECS] Track specifications and axis selectors (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-track-specs"></a>

An NSys visualization track specification MUST have the form `<track-kind>` or `<track-kind>:<selector>[,<selector>...]`.

A selector MUST have the form `<name>=<value>`.

The `device`, `stream`, and `context` selector values MUST be non-negative decimal integers unless a track kind explicitly permits `device=all`.

The `top` selector value MUST be a positive decimal integer.

The `depth` selector value MUST be a positive decimal integer.

The command MUST reject an invalid selector value with a structured diagnostic.

Track specifications MUST be parsed independently from one another.

Track-local selectors MUST take precedence over any command-level default selector with the same selector name.

The stable first-version track kind set MUST include `gpu`, `cuda-streams`, `cuda-stream`, `cuda-api`, `nvtx`, and `gaps-overlay`.

The `gpu` track kind MUST select aggregate GPU work for one or more devices.

The `cuda-streams` track kind MUST expand to CUDA stream tracks selected from one or more devices.

The `cuda-stream` track kind MUST select one exact CUDA stream.

The `cuda-api` track kind MUST select CPU-side CUDA Runtime and Driver API intervals.

The `nvtx` track kind MUST select NVTX ranges.

The `gaps-overlay` track kind MUST select GPU idle spans for overlay rendering rather than requiring a standalone lane.

A selector that names a CUDA stream MUST identify the parent CUDA device unless the track kind defines an unambiguous device expansion.

A selector that names a CUDA context MUST identify the parent CUDA device unless the track kind defines an unambiguous device expansion.

The command MUST reject a `cuda-stream` specification that contains `stream=<id>` without a unique device selector.

The command MUST reject unknown track kinds with a structured diagnostic.

The command MUST reject unknown selectors for a known track kind with a structured diagnostic.

The command MUST reject selector combinations that cannot resolve to a finite track set with a structured diagnostic.

The command SHOULD support `device=<id>` and `device=all` selectors for device-bearing track kinds.

The exact `cuda-stream` track kind MUST NOT accept `device=all`.

The command SHOULD support `top=<n>` for expansion track kinds whose natural expansion may be large.

The command SHOULD support `depth=<n>` for nested annotation track kinds such as `nvtx`.

**Rationale:** Nsight Systems timeline rows are hierarchical, not a flat lane list. Track specifications need enough axis information to avoid ambiguous stream and context identities while still allowing concise expansion such as top streams on a device.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-TRACK-TREE] Track tree resolution (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-track-tree"></a>

The `nsys viz timeline` command MUST resolve requested track specifications into a deterministic track tree before rendering.

Each rendered track row MUST have a stable `track_key`.

Each rendered track row MUST have a human-readable label.

Each rendered track row MUST have an explicit role.

The stable role set MUST include `group`, `summary`, `detail`, `annotation`, and `overlay`.

A `group` role row MUST represent hierarchy or ownership context rather than source intervals.

A `summary` role row MUST represent rollup evidence for a parent resource, such as GPU busy activity for one device.

A `detail` role row MUST represent concrete source intervals on a specific execution lane, such as a CUDA stream.

An `annotation` role row MUST represent explanatory or CPU-side context, such as CUDA API or NVTX ranges.

An `overlay` role item MUST represent derived explanatory evidence, such as idle gaps or selection windows, and MUST be visually distinguishable from ordinary source intervals.

Each rendered track row SHOULD carry source axes that identify the selected evidence, such as device, context, stream, process, thread, domain, or NVTX depth when those axes apply.

GPU-related track rows SHOULD be grouped under their owning device in the resolved track tree.

CUDA stream track rows SHOULD be grouped under their owning CUDA device.

CUDA context groupings MAY be present.

CPU API track rows SHOULD be grouped by process and thread when the selected evidence is thread-local.

NVTX track rows SHOULD carry the rendered depth for each displayed range row when a depth selector applies.

NVTX track row labels SHOULD include the nearest visible parent path when the requested depth is greater than one and the range has a visible parent.

Expansion track kinds MUST have deterministic ordering.

Top-N stream expansion SHOULD select streams by descending busy duration in the requested time window, then by device id, then by stream id.

The rendered track tree SHOULD display selected CUDA stream rows under their owning device group; within one device group, stream rows SHOULD preserve the selected stream order.

The response MUST report the number of requested track specifications.

The response MUST report the number of resolved track rows.

The response MUST report when requested tracks were omitted because of render limits.

The SVG MUST render track labels as a left-side tree with indentation that reflects parent-child relationships.

The SVG SHOULD visually distinguish group, summary, detail, annotation, and overlay roles.

Summary rows SHOULD be visually weaker than detail rows when both show the same underlying execution interval.

Summary rows SHOULD avoid default visible item labels that make rollup evidence look like a second concrete execution lane.

**Rationale:** Agents need the exported figure to explain why rows appear and how they relate. Nsight Systems presents rollup rows and detailed rows together, but the GUI has selection and correlation affordances that clarify duplicate appearances. A static VeloQ SVG needs explicit row roles and role-specific rendering so rollups, details, annotations, and overlays remain readable without interaction.

*Since: v0.1.0*

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-ARTIFACTS] SVG artifact and response contract (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-artifacts"></a>

The `nsys viz timeline` command MUST emit a VeloQ success envelope in JSON mode.

The success envelope MUST conform to VeloQ's success envelope contract.

The success payload MUST use VeloQ's canonical list shape.

The success payload `data.rows[]` MUST contain one primary figure row for each generated SVG artifact.

Each primary figure row MUST carry a `key`.

Each primary figure row key MUST identify the figure as an NSys timeline visualization.

Each primary figure row key MUST use the form `figure|timeline|<start_ns>..<end_ns>|req:<request_fingerprint>`.

The `<request_fingerprint>` component MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal string of at least 16 characters.

The `<request_fingerprint>` component MUST be derived from the resolved time window, requested track specifications, output-affecting render options, and output-affecting label options.

Each primary figure row key MUST be stable across equivalent requests over equivalent input evidence.

Each primary figure row MUST carry the SVG artifact `path`.

The primary figure row `path` field MUST be a string.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `format` with value `svg`.

Each primary figure row MUST carry the resolved `time_window_ns`.

The primary figure row `time_window_ns` field MUST be a two-element array of signed integer nanoseconds in `[start_ns, end_ns]` order.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `track_count`.

The primary figure row `track_count` field MUST be a non-negative integer.

The primary figure row `track_count` field MUST count resolved rendered track rows.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `rendered_item_count`.

The primary figure row `rendered_item_count` field MUST be a non-negative integer.

The primary figure row `rendered_item_count` field MUST count visual items emitted into the SVG.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `total_item_count`.

The primary figure row `total_item_count` field MUST be a non-negative integer.

The primary figure row `total_item_count` field MUST count selected source evidence items before item render limits are applied.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `aggregated`.

The primary figure row `aggregated` field MUST be a boolean.

The primary figure row `aggregated` field MUST be true when any selected evidence was represented by an aggregate visual item.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `omitted_track_count`.

The primary figure row `omitted_track_count` field MUST be a non-negative integer.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `suppressed_label_count`.

The primary figure row `suppressed_label_count` field MUST be a non-negative integer.

Each primary figure row MUST carry `truncated_label_count`.

The primary figure row `truncated_label_count` field MUST be a non-negative integer.

The success payload `data.auxiliary` MUST carry the requested track specifications.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.requested_tracks` field MUST be an array of strings.

The success payload `data.auxiliary` MUST carry the resolved track set.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.resolved_tracks` field MUST be an array of objects.

Each `data.auxiliary.resolved_tracks[]` object MUST carry `track_key`.

Each `data.auxiliary.resolved_tracks[]` object MUST carry `label`.

Each `data.auxiliary.resolved_tracks[]` object MUST carry `kind`.

Each `data.auxiliary.resolved_tracks[]` object MUST carry `role`.

The `role` field MUST identify the resolved track role using one of the stable role names defined by the track-tree contract.

Each `data.auxiliary.resolved_tracks[]` object SHOULD carry source axes when source axes apply to that track.

The success payload `data.auxiliary` MUST carry the effective render policy.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.render_policy` field MUST be an object.

The success payload `data.auxiliary` MUST carry the effective label policy.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.label_policy` field MUST be an object.

Each primary figure row MUST report whether aggregation, omission, label suppression, or label truncation occurred.

When `--out` is absent, the SVG artifact MUST be written under the VeloQ artifact root for the resolved NSys source path.

When `--out` is absent, the default SVG artifact path MUST be under a source-local `figures/nsys/timeline/` child of the artifact root.

When `--out` is present, the response MUST still identify the generated SVG path.

The command MUST NOT expose a partially written SVG artifact as a successful result.

The command MUST avoid leaving a corrupt partial SVG at the final output path after a handled failure when the destination filesystem permits atomic replacement.

The SVG artifact MUST NOT embed private absolute source paths, hostnames, or local machine identifiers unless the user explicitly requested those values in visible labels.

The SVG artifact MUST include non-private metadata for the VeloQ command, source kind, source version, resolved time window, resolved track keys, resolved track roles, render policy, and label policy used to create the figure.

**Rationale:** The SVG is a generated artifact, while stdout remains the agent-readable response. The row shape lets agents attach the figure to a report, check whether the figure is complete or aggregated, and clean generated files through the existing artifact lifecycle.

*Since: v0.1.0*

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-RENDER-LIMITS] Render limits and aggregation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-render-limits"></a>

The command MUST apply render limits before emitting the SVG artifact.

The command MUST have a maximum rendered track count.

The command MUST have a maximum rendered visual item count.

The command MUST report the effective render limits in the JSON response.

The command MUST report when the selected evidence exceeded a render limit.

The command MUST preserve a successful empty visualization as a success response rather than an error when the request is valid and no selected evidence overlaps the window.

The renderer MUST NOT silently stretch a short interval into a misleading long-duration rectangle solely to satisfy a minimum visible width.

Intervals whose screen width is below the minimum interval rendering threshold SHOULD be rendered as ticks, density marks, or aggregated bins.

Aggregated bins MUST visually distinguish aggregated evidence from individual intervals.

Aggregated bins MUST preserve metadata for the represented item count.

Aggregated bins MUST preserve metadata for the represented time span.

The command MUST document default render policy values for output width, maximum tracks, maximum items, minimum interval width, and aggregation behavior.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.render_policy.width_px` field MUST report output width in pixels.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.render_policy.max_tracks` field MUST report the maximum rendered track count.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.render_policy.max_items` field MUST report the maximum rendered visual item count.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.render_policy.min_interval_px` field MUST report the minimum interval rendering threshold in pixels.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.render_policy.aggregation` field MUST report the aggregation behavior.

The command MAY allow users to override render limits.

The command MUST reject render-limit overrides that would make the output unbounded.

**Rationale:** Static SVGs are only useful when the figure remains legible. Large traces can contain far more events than a report figure can show, so the command needs explicit limits and honest aggregation instead of rendering an unreadable or misleading image.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-LABEL-POLICY] Label and minimum-width policy (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-label-policy"></a>

The renderer MUST apply a label policy to visible item labels.

The label policy MUST distinguish item geometry visibility from item label visibility.

The label policy MUST have a minimum item-label width threshold.

The renderer MUST apply a documented label collision policy before emitting the SVG.

The label collision policy MUST prevent two visible item label boxes on the same rendered track row from overlapping horizontally.

The renderer MUST suppress visible item labels when the item is too narrow for the selected label mode.

The renderer MAY truncate visible item labels when the item is wide enough for a label but too narrow for the full label.

The command MUST report the effective label policy in the JSON response.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.label_policy.mode` field MUST report label mode.

The success payload `data.auxiliary.label_policy.min_label_px` field MUST report minimum item-label width in pixels.

The command MUST report the number of suppressed visible item labels.

The command MUST report the number of truncated visible item labels.

The SVG SHOULD preserve the full item name in an SVG metadata element or tooltip-compatible element when the full name is available.

The SVG SHOULD preserve the item row id or stable event reference in metadata when the item maps to a queryable NSys event.

Track labels MUST be governed separately from item labels.

Track labels MUST remain visible when the corresponding track row is rendered.

The command MAY support label modes such as automatic labels, no item labels, compact labels, and full labels.

A full-label mode MUST still preserve the non-overlap requirement.

The renderer SHOULD prefer short resolved names over demangled or fully qualified names for default visible item labels when a shorter resolved name is available.

**Rationale:** Kernel names, API names, and NVTX labels can be much longer than their visible intervals. A report figure should not become unreadable because labels collide, but the full evidence identity must remain available to agents and humans inspecting the SVG.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-SOURCE-ABSTRACTION] Source-neutral visualization boundary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-source-abstraction"></a>

This RFC MUST NOT be interpreted as specifying PyTorch visualization behavior.

This RFC MUST NOT be interpreted as specifying NCU visualization behavior.

NSys visualization track kinds and selectors MUST be treated as NSys source-specific contract.

Future sources that expose visualization commands MUST define their own command IDs, track kinds, selector semantics, response rows, artifact locations, and compatibility rules before those commands are treated as stable.

Source-specific evidence selection MUST remain owned by the source whose profile evidence is being visualized.

Rendering reuse MUST NOT cause PyTorch, NCU, or future sources to inherit NSys-specific axis hierarchy rules unless those rules are explicitly specified for that source.

Visualization output for one source MUST NOT depend on another source's track kinds, selectors, or axis hierarchy rules unless that dependency is explicitly specified for the producing source.

**Rationale:** A reusable visualization architecture is valuable, but the external contract belongs to each source. Keeping NSys track semantics source-specific lets the first implementation move quickly while preserving a clean boundary for future PyTorch visualization work.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-compatibility"></a>

Adding `nsys.viz.timeline` MUST NOT change the response shape of existing NSys commands.

Adding `nsys.viz.timeline` MAY keep the current NSys source version when existing NSys command responses remain compatible.

Changing the `nsys.viz.timeline` command ID after the command is stabilized MUST be treated as a breaking command-surface change.

Removing a stable track kind after the command is stabilized MUST be treated as a breaking visualization contract change.

Changing a stable selector's meaning after the command is stabilized MUST be treated as a breaking visualization contract change.

Removing a required field from the figure row after the command is stabilized MUST be treated as a breaking source payload change.

Changing the type or meaning of a required figure row field after the command is stabilized MUST be treated as a breaking source payload change.

Changing SVG visual styling MAY remain compatible when the required JSON response fields, track semantics, artifact lifecycle, and required SVG metadata semantics remain compatible.

Changing default render limits MAY remain compatible when the effective render limits are reported in the JSON response.

Adding new track kinds, selectors, optional response fields, or optional SVG metadata MAY remain compatible when existing behavior is preserved.

Adding a raw-SVG stdout mode MUST require an RFC amendment that documents the output exception.

**Rationale:** The figure command is additive to existing NSys query behavior, but once agents depend on it, command identity, track semantics, and response fields become part of the public source contract. Styling can evolve more freely than evidence semantics as long as the response tells agents what was rendered.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0009:C-HIGHLIGHT-POLICY] Highlight policy (Normative) <a id="rfc-0009c-highlight-policy"></a>

The `nsys viz timeline` command MAY support explicit highlight requests.

A highlight request MUST identify the source evidence set to highlight.

A top-kernel highlight request MUST define a positive top-K value.

A top-kernel highlight request MUST define whether ranking is over kernel names or concrete kernel instances.

When ranking over kernel names, the command MUST rank names using aggregate evidence within the resolved time window.

When ranking over concrete kernel instances, the command MUST rank individual kernel events within the resolved time window.

The default top-kernel ranking metric SHOULD be total kernel duration in the resolved time window.

The command MAY support additional ranking metrics such as count or maximum instance duration.

Highlight selection MUST be computed after the resolved time window and source axis filters are applied.

Highlight selection MUST NOT change which base intervals are selected for rendering.

Highlighted intervals MUST remain identifiable as their base event class, such as kernel, memcpy, CUDA API, or NVTX.

The SVG MUST visually distinguish highlighted intervals from non-highlighted intervals.

The SVG MUST NOT rely only on base event colors to communicate highlight membership.

The renderer SHOULD keep the base event-type legend separate from the highlight legend.

The highlight legend MUST identify each resolved highlight using a stable rank or label.

For top-kernel name highlights, the highlight legend SHOULD include the full kernel name when space permits.

When the full highlight name is too long for the visible legend, the SVG SHOULD visibly truncate or wrap it without overlapping other content.

The SVG MUST preserve the full highlight name in tooltip-compatible metadata or another SVG metadata element when a full name is available.

The success response MUST report the resolved highlight set when highlights are requested.

Each resolved highlight entry MUST report its rank or stable highlight id.

Each resolved highlight entry MUST report its display color or visual token.

Each resolved highlight entry MUST report the highlight scope, such as name or instance.

Each top-kernel name highlight entry MUST report the full kernel name.

Each top-kernel highlight entry SHOULD report aggregate metrics used for ranking, such as total duration, instance count, or maximum instance duration.

The command MUST report when a requested highlight resolved to no matching evidence.

A highlight request MUST be optional and MUST NOT affect the default timeline figure when omitted.

**Rationale:** Report figures often need to call attention to a small number of dominant kernels without losing base timeline semantics. Treating highlights as a separate visual layer lets agents explain top contributors while preserving the normal kernel/memcpy/API/NVTX legend and the source-owned timeline evidence contract from [RFC-0009](../rfc/RFC-0009.md).

*Since: v0.2.0*
